_comment: Repetition (cycle count) VLM config for vlm_run/run_vlm_repetitions.py, final_prompts set. Keys are NEVER stored here: each model names the environment variable that holds its API key. Relative paths resolve against the repo root. A key is read from the environment first, then from env_files (env_override true: the file wins over the shell). Command-line options override the values here.
_results_comment: One file per model and episode: <results_dir>/<experiment>/<model key>/<episode>/vlm_result.json. experiment: '' for trimmed MCAPs (three views), experiment_2 for head MP4s, experiment_3 for head+left+right MP4s (--wrists), experiment_4 for the chatgpt prompt set. --debug also keeps frames/, step_table.json and raw_response.json.

input._comment: Head-camera MP4s (head view only) or trimmed delivery MCAPs (three synchronized views). The MCAP camera roles come from the recording metadata. With --wrists, <ep>_left.mp4 and <ep>_right.mp4 next to the head file are used too.

frames._comment: The fixed step grid of final_prompts: one step every 1/fps seconds on the shared timeline, the same instant in every view. The model answers in these step numbers only; code maps steps to seconds (step table). Identical for every model.
frames._label_note: Each image is preceded by its label, as repetition_system.json describes: 'f003_head | camera head | t = 0.40 s | step 3'.

prompt._note: repetition_system.json is the system turn. The user turn opens with the episode prompt (episode_id, context, steps, image_order) with the output contract inside it, then the labelled images in step order (head, wrist_left, wrist_right per step). The versions of the three files are written into every result. The chatgpt set has its own file names and builds its own step numbering (no step->time mapping); it is kept only for comparison.

gemini-3.8-flash._media_resolution_note: Gemini 3 image tokens: low about 280, medium 560, high 1120 per image. Measured on episode_000007 (128 head images): high 145,121 input tokens; low 42,976 (34,048 image = 266 per image, 8,928 text). Low + batch on 2026-11-24: 3 cycles, $0.0254, 246 s.
gemini-3.8-flash._price_note: USD per 1M tokens [input, output incl. thinking], introductory until 2026-12-31; from 2027-01-01 live $1.50/$7.50 and batch $0.75/$3.75 (update both).

deepseek-v4.1-flash._provider_note: null: any OpenRouter provider that takes images (DeepInfra, the bench config's pin, serves this model text-only).
deepseek-v4.1-flash._reasoning_note: medium spent all 40,000 output tokens on reasoning and returned no answer on episode_000007 (2026-11-24); low leaves room for the JSON.
deepseek-v4.1-flash._price_note: measured from OpenRouter's reported cost on 2026-11-24 (44,066 input + 40,000 output = $0.0245); OpenRouter also returns usage.cost per call, which is what the result records.

batch._comment: Gemini Batch API (models/<model>:batchGenerateContent) with inline requests: all episodes of one call in one job while the request stays under inline_limit_mb (about 2 head-only episodes of 128 steps, 9.7 MB each); otherwise run fewer episodes per call. Batch is half the live price and finishes in minutes to 24 h. A job can be resumed with --batch-name batches/<id>. countTokens (free) runs before submit and prints the input cost.

checks._comment: Code checks after each response, from the output contract: flags only, the model count is never edited.
